src: APPSC Group-II Prelims 2024 (25-02-2024)
s:
Consider the following statements about the Indira Gandhi Prize for Peace, Disarmament and Development for 2023:

I. Daniel Barenboim was announced as winner of the Indira Gandhi Prize for 2023 for his efforts to solve economic crisis and his contribution in the development of Sri Lanka.

II. Ali Abu Awwad was announced as winner of the Indira Gandhi Prize 2023 for his efforts towards a non-violent resolution of the Israel-Palestine conflict.

III. The International Jury of the Indira Gandhi Prize for Peace, Disarmament and Development for 2023 was chaired by former Chief Justice of India, R.M. Lodha.
Which among the above given statements are incorrect?
x: The 2023 Indira Gandhi Prize went jointly to Barenboim and Ali Abu Awwad for Israel-Palestine peace efforts (not Sri Lanka), and the jury was chaired by T.S. Thakur, not R.M. Lodha, so I and III are incorrect.

src: UPSC CSE Prelims 2026
s: 'X', born in the UK, was conferred the Nobel Prize in 2025. He was a professor in an American university when this prize was announced. Identify 'X'.
x: John Clarke was born in Cambridge, UK, and was a professor at the University of California, Berkeley when he was awarded the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics. He shared the prize with Michel H. Devoret (born in France) and John M. Martinis (born in the US) for the discovery of macroscopic quantum mechanical tunnelling and energy quantisation in an electric circuit. • Note: Questions of this nature are often designed by UPSC to maintain unpredictability and keep the cutoff balanced. x: The 58th Jnanpith (2023) was shared by Gulzar (Sampooran Singh Kalra) and Jagadguru Rambhadracharya, so I and II are correct. Damodar Mauzo won the 57th (2022), so III is wrong.

src: APPSC Group-1 PYQ
s: Which one of the following is not a recipient of Jnanpith Award?
x: Prof. Amartya Sen, the Nobel laureate economist, has not been a recipient of the Jnanpith Award, which is given for excellence in Indian literature, not economics. The other three named individuals are recognised Telugu and Assamese literary figures who received the award. The Jnanpith is India's highest literary honour.

src: Uttarakhand PCS (Pre) 2024
s: Besides Urdu poet Gulzar, who is the other recipient of the 58th Jnanpith Award ?
x: The Jnanpith Award is an annual Indian literary award. It was established in 1961. It is awarded only to Indian citizens who write in the languages included in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution and English. The 58th Jnanpith Award for 2023 was jointly conferred upon Gulzar, a renowned figure in Hindi cinema and a highly esteemed Urdu poet, and Rambhadracharya, a famous Hindu spiritual guru, teacher, and writer. The 2022 Jnanpith Award was presented to Goan writer Damodar Mauzo.

src: State PSC
s: Who has been given the Jnanpith Award for the year 2015 ?
x: The Jnanpith Award (51st) of the year 2015 was presented to the renowned writer of Gujarati language, Raghuveer Chaudhari. Sanskrit Scholar Jagadguru Rambhadracharya and Urdu poet and lyricist Gulzar have been chosen for the 58th Jnanpith Award.

src: CDS 2015
s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

I. Professor Komal Bawa was conferred with the MIDORI Prize (2014) for biodiversity for his research on climate change in the himalayas.

II. MIDORI Prize is an annual international prize given to an individual for outstanding contribution to the conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity at global regional or local level.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x:
Official key / most books: both I and II. Strictly: the MIDORI Prize is biennial, not annual, so statement II is loose (AEON Environmental Foundation / CBD Secretariat).
Kamal Bawa (ATREE) won the 2014 MIDORI Prize for Biodiversity, his work including climate change in the Himalayas, and the prize honours individuals for conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity at global, regional or local level – the CDS key is 'both'. Strictly the prize is biennial, not annual.
